content_of_post_to_comment:
I'm going straight to the point, I've always felt left out. Ive been to therapy, and this year some things happened to my family one of them being my dad moving out. After that the truth is I expected my friends to normally want to be there for me, I truly really had high expectations apparently because after a message or two checking in on me I was the one that kept contact acting them. After a few months of me being always the one texting first I simply stopped doing it, now we don't talk, I don't talk to almost nobody outside my family.

Today a family friend is celebrating her birthday, for some reason she never directly invites me but always assumes I'll go, I hate that, I've told her that.

Now this year my friends got invited and I found out through Find my Phone. My friends are going, my siblings are going I know i'm welcomed at the house because the parents are my godparents, so I'm wondering should I just say fuck it and just go?

I just feel like I constantly feel sorry for myself for feeling alone everyday but I never just say fuck it.

Should I just go?
comment: Honestly, I think there's a difference between showing up for yourself and pretending nothing hurt. If you want to go to the birthday, go because you want to spend time with people you care about, not to prove you still belong. Also, your friends going quiet after your dad moved out sounds painful, but sometimes people don't realize how much support someone needs unless we tell them directly.
